newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $67-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $67-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales turned active near midday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area at $67.00 per cwt, unchanged from most of last week's sales, feedlot sources said.

About 45,000 head sold in the Panhandle as of mid- afternoon, bringing the week-to-date figure near 84,000, sources said. In Kansas, about 30,000 head sold, which brought the week-to-date number near 46,000, Kansas sources said.
Owners had priced cattle at $68.00 but accepted lower bids in the face of falling beef prices Wednesday and perceptions that packer buying would thin before the Easter weekend.
However, some owners continued to pass packer bids at $67.00, holding out for $68.00 amid ideas beef demand would rebound following the holiday weekend, sources said.
"I would rather carry my cattle over," one Texas cattle owner said.
A relatively large number of cattle on the Kansas showlist and a marginal number on the Panhandle list will be carried over to next week, they said.
This week's Panhandle showlist was pegged near 95,000 head and the Kansas list near 85,000.

USDA pegged Thursday's closing boxed beef prices down another $0.40 to $0.69 per cwt on 315 loads of fabricated cuts sold. The slide followed Wednesday's drop in values which ranged from $0.45 to $0.96 lower.
